Roth GraphER reranking for RAG is not directly addressed by the supplied papers, but the closest match is GraphER [1], which is a graph-based enrichment and reranking framework for retrieval-augmented generation. [1] It builds a query-time graph from proximity relationships and applies graph-based ranking to surface top candidate documents, with improved retrieval completeness and no extra graph infrastructure. [1]

If you meant reranking more generally, LURE-RAG [4], RRPO [3], and RSRank [9] also focus on RAG reranking, but they optimize different goals: utility-driven ordering, LLM-feedback alignment, and relevance scoring from representational shift, respectively. [3, 4, 9]
